proposed_assumptions.claim: For an illustrative uniform clock, propose t(n)=n tau with tau>0 and [tau]=time. This rule is additional to the source.
Use x(n+1)-x(n) and t(n+1)-t(n) to define a discrete step velocity. Interpreting it as physical propagation requires a further physical interpretation and clock calibration.

established_derivations.derivation: For every n, delta x=L and delta t=tau. The proposed discrete step velocity is v=L/tau, with units length/time. If L is a positive length scale, its speed magnitude is L/tau; generally the magnitude of the signed step velocity is abs(L)/tau.
established_derivations.claim_scope: Conditional on the proposed clock and definition.

established_derivations.derivation: Two admissible proposed intervals tau and 2 tau produce step ratios L/tau and L/(2 tau) while preserving the same position sequence. Therefore the position source cannot identify a unique speed when L is nonzero. Even for L=0, a clock is needed to define a time-based velocity.
